newsitem.title: UK: LME seeks change to open interest/position reports.
newsitem.headline: LME seeks change to open interest/position reports.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) is proposing to change its method of reporting open interest data, as well as moving further towards automated large position reporting.
In a notice to members the LME said that as part of implementing the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) review it was looking at its current system of reporting open interest.

"It is believed that while the method...which has been in use for the reporting of LME business for many years is considered adequate, the system could be significantly enhanced by the adoption of the new procedures," it said.
The new system is intended to be operational by about June 1998.

Currently, the LME reports open interest by currency, as though each commodity/currency combination is a different commodity. This should be changed to ignore the differing currencies and only reflect metal positions.
Also, the current method of calculating open interest ignores the effect of member's positions with their clients, including affiliate companies, or their own proprietary positions.

"One consequence of this is that the turnover figures may show high volumes of trading, but with no change in open interest because the trading is all conducted with clients and recorded as crosses," the LME said.

Under the proposed new method, open interest will be calculated by aggregating by members the net uncovered position of every client, including affiliates and proprietary positions, to create the member's open interest.
So that systems developments at the LME and at member companies can be progressed in an orderly way, membership views are sought by the end of August.
Meanwhile, views on electronically transmitting large position reporting data are being called for by the end of this month.
The LME's target launch date for implenting this is the end of 1997.
